title: multitenant-gpu-consolidation-exercise-notes
content:
Context:
Customer: Customer Sigma (finance vertical), wants to consolidate 3 internal ML teams onto a single Dedicated pool to reduce spend and simplify ops. Current state: each team runs independent single-model endpoints on A100-like instances, overprovisioned for peaks. Goal for POC: demonstrate safe consolidation with predictable latency SLO (p95 < 350ms), cost reduction target >= 30% vs current committed spend, and an autoscale policy that prevents noisy-neighbor regressions.

High-level approach:
- Build a small multi-tenant pool (initially 2 x A100-80GB equiv) with per-tenant QoS controls and predictable routing rules.
- Implement workload-aware autoscaler that considers active KV cache hit-rate, current token/sec, and per-route latency headroom.
- Run a 48h stress experiment with synthetic and recorded traffic from each team; measure p50/p95, throughput, and token cost.

Assumptions and inputs we used for quick math (POC assumptions, make explicit to customer):
- Model mix: 70% chat/complete requests (avg 220 tokens/request), 30% embeddings (avg 512-d vectors, 1.6k tokens/request equivalent compute).
- Median concurrent sessions pre-POC: team A: 120, team B: 45, team C: 30 -> aggregate median concurrency ~195. Peak concurrency: +2.5x burst factor -> ~490.
- Per-GPU sustained throughput: A100-80GB baseline approx 2000 tokens/sec for chat model (quantized int8 path), embedding model throughput higher due to shorter context; we conservatively treat embedding CPU+GPU pipeline as equivalent to 1500 tokens/sec.
- KV cache expected hit-rate: 12% (workload has some repetition), prefix caching reduces token generation by approx 10% effective.
- Cost estimates used: A100-80GB equivalent purchased on Dedicated pool: $2.80/hr (effective blended cost after reserved discount). H100-like: $5.90/hr (note: numbers are illustrative for customer discussion).

Quick consolidation cost simulation (6-month window):
- Baseline (current): each team separate; effective committed hours: 3 x 24/7 x 1 GPU = 3 * 24 * 30 * 6 = 12,960 GPU-hours. At $2.80/hr -> $36,288.
- Consolidated pool initial commit: 2 GPUs baseline, with autoscale up to 5 for burst windows. Steady-state expected commit to hit SLA: 2 GPUs * 24*30*6 = 8640 GPU-hours -> $24,192.
- Estimated autoscale burst delta (additional hours for month-long simulation): approx 700 extra GPU-hours -> $1,960.
- Total expected 6-month spend (consolidated) ~ $26,152 -> ~28% reduction vs baseline.
- Sensitivity: If median concurrency shifts +20%, autoscale adds 1 permanent GPU and costs rise ~12% (clear knob to monitor).

Autoscale policy proposal (POC config idea):
- Metrics: primary = aggregate_inflight_requests (per-second smoothed), secondary = observed_p95_latency (sliding window 5m), tertiary = KV_cache_hit_rate.
- Scale-up rules: +1 GPU when inflight > 180 per GPU_capacity_threshold OR observed_p95_latency > target_latency * 1.15 for 3 consecutive 30s windows.
- Scale-down rules: -1 GPU when inflight < 90 per GPU for 10m and p95_latency < target_latency * 0.9 and cache_hit_rate stable (>8%).
- Cooldown: 5m on scale-up, 15m on scale-down for stability.
- Max concurrency per GPU target: 220 concurrent generation sessions (~safe headroom for tail-latency bursts).
- Canary rule: if p95 > 450ms for two minutes after a scale event, trigger automated rollback to last-known-good routing (route heavy teams to reserved lane or hosted fallback).

QoS / tenant isolation controls (recommended):
- Per-tenant route weight: reserve guaranteed slots (e.g., team A=55% baseline concurrency reservation, B=25%, C=20%) enforced by request admission at the routing layer.
- Token rate limits per-tenant to protect throughput during storms.
- Soft-priority queues: promote latency-sensitive short requests, batchable embedding requests placed in lower priority queue to increase batching efficiency.
- Fallbacks: define per-tenant fallback to smaller quantized model or hosted API in case of sustained quota exceed.

Experiment plan (POC runbook):
1) Week 0 - prep: ingest real recent traffic traces (anonymized), synthetic generator scripts, baseline SLO dashboard. Baseline CPU/GPU perf runs with sample payloads.
2) Week 1 - small closed traffic run: 2 GPUs, 24h, low burst. Validate latency and cost telemetry, tune admission control.
3) Week 2 - scaled stress: introduce peak bursts (2.5x) and KV-cache warm/cold dynamics, measure autoscale reaction and tail latency.
4) Week 3 - tenant shuffle + failure injection: kill one GPU, simulate network hiccups, ensure graceful degradation (route to hosted or fall back to smaller model).
5) Week 4 - report and handoff: run extended 48h replicant, produce final TCO and recommendations.

Runbook checklist for engineers (play-by-play during run):
- verify admin keys and tenant bindings are correct
- enable token-level billing and per-route tracing for first 24h
- run eviction/GC probe to confirm KV cache sizes and eviction rate under load
- continuous perf dashboard (p50/p95/p99, queue depth, batch sizes, GPU util%)
- after each major test, snapshot model KV-state, config, and load generator seed for reproducibility

Preliminary observations from lab experiments (notes):
- Multi-tenant batching gained ~14% throughput due to cross-tenant batch packing for embeddings (unexpected but repeatable in lab).
- Noisy-tenant effect visible when Team A runs long-chat sessions with >2k tokens — this drove p99 spikes; admission control prevented spillover.
- Quantized int8 performance for chat model reduced per-token compute by ~1.6x but increased variance on long sequences; choose hybrid: int8 for short/medium sequences, fp16 for long chat flows.

Open questions for customer workshop:
- Are there hard regulatory constraints that force per-tenant hardware isolation? If yes, consolidation will be limited to logical isolation only.
- Acceptable fallback mix: hosted fallback acceptable for non-PII traffic? (we need explicit approval).
- Upcoming model changes: customer expecting to onboard a 70B dense model in next quarter — should influence longer-term capacity commit.

Suggested deliverables for POC proposal doc to customer:
- 2-page SLA and autoscale behavior summary (visual diagrams)
- 1-page cost sensitivity chart (+/- concurrency and GPU price)
- 1-runbook appendix with step-by-step escalation and rollback actions
- 48h lab report with perf traces and config snapshots

Action items (owners):
- Sofia: assemble the 48h traffic synth (deadline 2024-08-19)
- Raj: implement autoscale prototype (PR link above) and add canary rollback hook (deadline 2024-08-23)
- Lina: build dashboard (alerts for p95 > 350ms, queue depth > 500, cache_hit_rate drop > 5pp) and initial runbook text (2024-08-20)
- Marcus: prepare sample cost sheet for customer including H100 vs A100 scenarios (2024-08-21)

Notes-to-self: keep the POC conservative on scale-down to avoid oscillation; emphasize observability (traces + per-token cost attribution) in proposal. Also, include example curl snippets for tenant routing and the hosted fallback test in the final appendix.

End of notes.
